title: Piece values depend on the position

D0.outcome: States the usual point scale as a starting estimate and gives two reasons it changes (mobility, structure).

D1.outcome: Given a position with pieces of unequal mobility, decides which of two pieces to keep and gives the positional reason.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, judges trades such as an exchange sacrifice or bishop against rook with pawns using position-dependent values, including a rook that has no file to enter.

D3.outcome: Predicts how one feature (a file opening, pieces coming off, a locked structure) changes the value of a piece, and does not use numeric force tables from the sources.

misconceptions: A rook is always worth more than a minor piece.
sources: sources/sheets/znosko-borovsky_middle-game.md §5 item 1 (numeric force values: do not use)
conditions: In ordinary open or semi-open positions the usual ordering holds; mobility is the main driver of value.
Comparisons are pairwise, not a single table.
contrasts: A rook with no open file to enter gains nothing from winning the exchange.
Queen and knight may beat queen and bishop.
Using the force table with pawn units from the Z-B text.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.EXCHANGE.D2: trade decisions use the changed values
